hens_rule_text: Columbus code text found in search extracts limits fowl-keeping to lots of two acres or more; on a qualifying lot the cap is one "bird unit" per acre, with a bird unit defined as 32 chickens (or 16 ducks, or 8 turkeys/geese). Ordinary residential lots under 2 acres appear not to qualify at all.
permit_notes: No permit process was found; eligibility instead turns on lot size (2+ acres), which functions like a zoning threshold rather than a permit.
setback_notes: Search extracts of the code state barns or structures for keeping/confining poultry must be at least 100 ft from any lot line, not specifically from a neighbor's dwelling.
coop_rules: Structures used to keep or shelter poultry must sit at least 100 ft from any property line; only fowl six weeks or older count toward the per-acre cap.
zoning_notes: Chapter 5 (Animals and Fowl) of the Columbus consolidated government code appears to treat fowl-keeping as an accessory agricultural use requiring a 2+ acre lot, which excludes most ordinary single-family residential parcels.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Sec. 5-7.1 (section number uncertain; possibly renumbered, one summary cited Sec. 5-42)

sources.name: Chapter 5 - Animals and Fowl, Code of Ordinances, Columbus, GA (Municode)

research_notes: Municode's Columbus page returned a 403 (region block) on direct and Wayback fetch attempts, so all code language here comes from search-engine text extracts that quote the ordinance, not a page I read directly. The exact code section number is inconsistent between two search results (5-7.1 vs 5-42), so it is flagged as uncertain. The core fact (2-acre minimum, 32-chicken bird unit, no roosters) appeared consistently across the extract, but this needs direct verification.
